paragraphs.text: Three-level source-text pins for DeepSeek Harness that survive context compaction: recall on demand,
resident background, or highlighted constraints.
# highlightpin
**Pin any selected passage; compaction cannot take it away.**
中文 · Design · Evaluation · Live evidence
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. Select any stretch of text in a conversation — a constraint, a numb
er, a formula, a piece of code — and pin it with one click. From then on, no matter how the context
is compacted, what the model receives is that **source text**, not a summary.
## Three levels
Each pin carries its own level:
| Level | Behaviour | Good for | Cost |
| **pin** (default) | Does nothing while the text is still in context; once compaction drops it, the
extract text is re-inserted verbatim near the tail before the next request | Most pins | Never touc

hes the system prompt, so it does not break the prefix cache on its own |
| **resident** | Lives in
the system prompt with neutral wording: "consult it when relevant; no need to bring it up" | Importa
nt background: you want the model to match on it the moment it matters, without you mentioning it ev

ery turn | Costs one prefix-cache invalidation when you switch levels |
| **highlight** | Lives in t
he system prompt with emphatic wording: "follow it when relevant; if it conflicts with your latest e
xplicit instruction, the latest instruction wins" | Constraints and priorities the model must keep h
onouring | Same as above; emphasis also raises how often the model brings it up on its own |
`resident` and `highlight` are deliberately two separate levels. "The model can always find it" and
"the model always keeps it in mind" are different things, and emphasis has side effects of its own —
so the choice is yours.

### Compatible DSH versions
`peerDependencies` declares `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`. The DSH plugin manager
checks these peers with `semver.satisfies(runtimeVersion, range, { includePrerelease: true })` and
blocks installation and activation on a mismatch.
The range carries an explicit prerelease branch on purpose: under ordinary semver semantics a single
`>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` does not match the `0.2.0-rc.*` builds, because node-semver admits a prerel
ease only when some comparator in the range shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple and itself ca
rries a prerelease tag.

very push |

nsupported**: `CommandDefinitionId` does not exist at 0.1.5 and below, and the 0.1.6 line's session-

## Usage

1. Select text inside **one** finished user or assistant message.
2. Click the pin above the compose

r.
3. Click the arrow beside it to open the details panel: switch each pin between "recall / residen
t / highlight", check budget usage, or unpin.
When you select inside a formula, the selection is expanded to the whole formula and what gets store
d is the TeX source. Select the rendered $\nabla_\theta J(\theta)$ and the plugin stores `$\nabla_\t
heta J(\theta)$` — not the glyphs on screen. Selections inside code keep their indentation and line
\theta)$` — not the glyphs on screen. Selections inside code keep their indentation and line breaks.
Everything is also available from the command line:
| Command | Effect |

| `/hlpin list` | List every pin, its level and budget usage |
| `/hlpin last` | Pin the most recent

assistant reply in full |
| `/hlpin show <n>` | Show one pin's full text |
| `/hlpin drop <n>` | Un

pin |
| `/hlpin level <n> pin\|resident\|highlight` | Change a pin's level |
## Design notes
- **What is stored is source text, not screen text.** The client serialises the selection first (for
mulas back to TeX, copy buttons and line numbers stripped out), and the host then locates the matchi
ng source substring in the session log. Alignment reports one of three fidelities: `source-exact` (a
clean hit), `source-normalized` (matched after whitespace and Markdown normalisation, but still sto

ring a source slice), or `rendered` (no match — it stores the display text and **tells you so**).
-
**`pin` only re-inserts after the original is gone.** Right after pinning, the text is already in co
ntext, so re-injecting it would be pointless. It comes back only once compaction has shadowed it — a
nd at that moment the prefix cache was already invalidated. So the default level cannot break cachin

g by construction.
- **The decision is a pure function that keeps no ledger.** Every step re-decides
from "is this text still in context", and records nothing like "already re-inserted". A rejected st
ep, a plugin restart, or the recall notice itself being compacted later therefore cannot lose a pin.
- **The resident section and the recall notice never duplicate each other.** Each step records whic
h pins actually went into the system prompt for that step, and the recall path excludes them. With n

o such record it re-inserts as usual: better to duplicate than to lose.
- **Over budget means reject
ion, not truncation.** `pin`, `resident` and `highlight` each have their own character pool. Adding
or promoting past a pool's budget is rejected outright with an error code; demotion is always allowe

d. The plugin never quietly truncates, evicts, or demotes a pin.
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- Selections must stay within a single message; cross-message selections are not supported.
- Stream

ing messages, reasoning content and tool output are not supported.
- Pins belong to one session; for

ked sessions do not inherit them.
- One writer host per profile is supported.
- "Highlight" here is
an emphasis level in the model input; it does not draw a visual highlight on the original message.
